subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 3-year-old child of Asian descent has moderate to severe microcytic hypochromic anemia and splenomegaly. Peripheral smear shows target cells. Hemoglobin electrophoresis reveals a fast-migrating hemoglobin tetramer. Genetic testing shows deletion of three of the four alpha-globin genes on chromosome 16.
question: Which of the following hemoglobin tetramers is most likely present in excess in this child?
explanation_correct: Deletion of three alpha-globin genes causes hemoglobin H disease. With only one functional alpha gene, alpha-globin synthesis is severely reduced and the excess beta-globin chains assemble into beta4 tetramers called HbH. This produces a moderate to severe microcytic hypochromic anemia with target cells and splenomegaly. By contrast, deletion of all four alpha genes causes hemoglobin Barts disease with gamma4 tetramers and hydrops fetalis. Alpha-thalassemia is especially prevalent in people of Asian and African descent.

explanation_incorrect.A: HbA requires two alpha chains, so it is markedly reduced rather than increased in HbH disease.
explanation_incorrect.B: HbF also requires alpha chains and is not the excess tetramer when three alpha genes are deleted.
explanation_incorrect.D: Hb Barts is the gamma4 tetramer that occurs when all four alpha-globin genes are deleted, causing hydrops fetalis.
explanation_incorrect.E: HbA2 is a minor adult hemoglobin composed of alpha2 delta2 and is characteristically elevated in beta-thalassemia trait, not HbH disease.

educationalObjective: Three alpha-globin gene deletions cause HbH disease with excess beta4 tetramers; four deletions cause Hb Barts (gamma4).

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A healthy 24-year-old has a routine CBC showing hemoglobin 14.2 g/dL, MCV 88 fL, and RBC count 5.0 million per microliter. He has no symptoms or family history of anemia. Genetic testing reveals a single alpha-globin gene deletion on chromosome 16; the other three alpha genes are intact.
question: Which of the following is the correct diagnosis for this patient?
explanation_correct: A single alpha-globin gene deletion produces alpha-thalassemia minima, also called the silent carrier state, with no anemia and normal red cell indices. The normal genotype is alpha alpha/alpha alpha, so one deletion leaves three functional alpha genes, which is sufficient for normal hemoglobin synthesis. Two deletions produce alpha-thalassemia minor with a mild microcytic hypochromic anemia. Three deletions cause HbH disease and four cause Hb Barts disease with hydrops fetalis.

explanation_incorrect.B: Alpha-thalassemia minor results from two alpha-globin gene deletions, either cis or trans, and causes a mild microcytic anemia rather than normal indices.
explanation_incorrect.C: Hemoglobin H disease requires three alpha-gene deletions and causes moderate to severe microcytic anemia with beta4 tetramers.
explanation_incorrect.D: Hemoglobin Barts disease requires all four alpha genes to be deleted and causes hydrops fetalis incompatible with life.
explanation_incorrect.E: Iron deficiency anemia would show low ferritin, elevated TIBC, and microcytic hypochromic cells, not an isolated alpha-globin gene deletion with normal iron studies.

educationalObjective: One alpha-globin gene deletion produces silent carrier status (alpha-thalassemia minima) with no anemia; two deletions produce thalassemia minor.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A fetus at 28 weeks' gestation has severe pallor, generalized edema, and hepatosplenomegaly on ultrasound. Hemoglobin analysis demonstrates a tetramer composed of four gamma-globin chains with essentially no alpha-globin. Genetic testing confirms deletion of all four alpha-globin genes. The counseling team discusses the prognosis with the parents.
question: Which of the following statements about this hemoglobin and condition is correct?

options.text: The gamma4 tetramer is HbH and is compatible with survival into adulthood with transfusions
The gamma4 tetramer results from a point mutation in the beta-globin gene on chromosome 11
This pattern is expected with three alpha-gene deletions, a condition known as HbH disease
Excess beta-globin chains form the gamma4 tetramer in this disorder
The gamma4 tetramer is Hb Barts and causes hydrops fetalis that is incompatible with life

explanation_correct: Deletion of all four alpha-globin genes abolishes alpha-chain production, so excess fetal gamma-globin chains assemble into gamma4 tetramers called hemoglobin Barts. Hb Barts binds oxygen very tightly and cannot deliver it effectively to tissues, causing severe fetal anemia, high-output heart failure, generalized edema, and hydrops fetalis. This condition is incompatible with life, with affected fetuses typically dying in utero or shortly after birth. It is most frequent in populations of Asian and African descent, which is why carrier screening is important in these groups.

explanation_incorrect.A: HbH is the beta4 tetramer seen with three alpha-gene deletions; Hb Barts is gamma4 with four deletions and is not compatible with survival.
explanation_incorrect.B: This is a deletion disorder of the alpha-globin genes on chromosome 16, not a beta-globin point mutation on chromosome 11 as in beta-thalassemia.
explanation_incorrect.C: Three deletions cause HbH disease with beta4 tetramers; this fetus has four deletions and gamma4 Hb Barts.
explanation_incorrect.D: With no alpha-globin produced, it is the excess gamma-globin chains in the fetus that form gamma4; beta4 tetramers occur in HbH disease with three deletions.

educationalObjective: Four alpha-gene deletions cause Hb Barts (gamma4), producing hydrops fetalis that is incompatible with life.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 35-year-old man of African descent has hemoglobin 11.9 g/dL, MCV 70 fL, and RBC count 5.7 million per microliter. Ferritin, serum iron, and TIBC are all normal. Peripheral smear shows target cells. Genetic testing shows two alpha-globin gene deletions, one on each chromosome 16 (a trans deletion pattern).
question: Which of the following diagnoses and mechanisms best fit these findings?

options.text: Iron deficiency anemia due to chronic blood loss
Alpha-thalassemia minor with a trans deletion and mild microcytic anemia
Hemoglobin H disease with excess beta4 tetramers
Anemia of chronic disease with low TIBC

explanation_correct: Two alpha-globin gene deletions cause alpha-thalassemia minor, producing a mild microcytic hypochromic anemia. The deletions can be cis, both on the same chromosome, or trans, one on each chromosome as in this patient. A relatively high RBC count for the degree of anemia, target cells, normal iron studies, and ancestry of Asian or African descent favor thalassemia trait over iron deficiency; the Mentzer index would typically be below 13. Three deletions would cause HbH disease and four would cause Hb Barts disease.

explanation_incorrect.A: Iron deficiency would show low ferritin, elevated TIBC, and a low or normal RBC count, not normal iron studies with an elevated RBC count and a documented gene deletion.
explanation_incorrect.C: Hemoglobin H disease requires three alpha-gene deletions and produces moderate to severe anemia with beta4 tetramers, not two deletions and mild anemia.
explanation_incorrect.D: Beta-thalassemia minor is caused by a beta-globin point mutation on chromosome 11 with elevated HbA2, not by alpha-gene deletions on chromosome 16.
explanation_incorrect.E: Anemia of chronic disease shows low serum iron, low TIBC, and high ferritin; this patient's iron studies are normal.

educationalObjective: Alpha-thalassemia minor (two deletions, cis or trans) causes mild microcytosis with a high RBC count and normal iron studies, unlike iron deficiency.
